I haven't changed anything yet. One part of this isn't covered by the Design Kit, and the project rules say to stop and ask in that case.

**What's covered:** The Design Kit is the vendored folder `design-kit/`. It defines a Card component (`design-kit/components/card.html`) and a primary Button (`design-kit/components/button.html`). The new card's markup, title, text and "Browse events" button can be copied from those exactly, the same way the "Your bookings" card was built.

**What's missing:** The kit says nothing about the space between two cards stacked one above the other. Today the page has one card, so this never came up. The card component has no outer margin, and the kit has no layout or "stack" component.

**How each option plays out** (the "Upcoming events" card placed under "Your bookings"):

- **A. Extend the kit first (recommended).** You add a spacing rule to the Design Kit, for example "stacked cards: gap `--space-4`", and re-export it. I then copy that value into `styles.css`. The result: the cards are separated by exactly the value the kit defines, and future pages follow the same rule.
- **B. I pick an existing token now.** I use `gap: var(--space-4)` (16px) on `<main>`. The result: 16px between the cards, which looks consistent with the card's own inner padding (also 16px). But the value is my choice, not the kit's, so it could disagree with what the design team later defines. That's "kit drift".
- **C. No gap.** The cards touch. The result: the shadow of the first card runs into the second card, and they read as one broken block. That's "touching cards".

| Option | Spacing source | Follows kit rule | Work for you | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Extend kit | Design Kit | Yes | Add one rule to the kit | None |
| B. Existing token | My choice (`--space-4`) | No | None | Kit drift |
| C. No gap | n/a | Yes, but looks broken | None | Touching cards |

**Recommendation: A.** The rule exists so the page never contains values the kit doesn't define. Cost: you have to update the kit before I can finish. If you need the card today, B is a reasonable stand-in that you can align with the kit later.

Once this is decided, I'll also need a Linear issue ID for the commit message. I'll work on a new branch, not `main`.
